wars.name: Battle of Plassey and the conquest of Bengal
wars.outcome: British victory on 23 June 1757; Mir Jafar made Nawab and Bengal a British puppet state.
wars.note: Treaty signed 4 June 1757; the page dates the deposition of Mir Jafar to after the battle of Chinsura (25 November 1759), which is not otherwise dated here.

wars.name: Battle of Buxar and the Treaty of Allahabad
wars.outcome: Buxar on 22 October 1764; the Treaty of Allahabad of 16 August 1765 gave the Company the diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa, returned Awadh to Shuja-ud-Daula minus Allahabad and Kora, and left Awadh dependent.
wars.note: No contest zone: the Company did not take Awadh; Allahabad and Kora went to the Mughal emperor.

wars.name: First Anglo-Mysore War

zones.text: Karur, which the Treaty of Madras left to Mysore

wars.outcome: Hyder Ali nearly captured Madras; the Treaty of Madras of 29 March 1769 'restored the status quo ante bellum, except for Mysore's acquisition of Karur' and pledged mutual defence.
wars.note: The Company page dates the first war to 1766 in the body and 1767 in the infobox. Repair: First_Anglo-Mysore_War has the war beginning in January 1767 and ending with the Treaty of Madras on 29 March 1769 (it does not mention Karur); Hyder_Ali gives the Karur clause. No page names Karur's earlier holder.

wars.name: First Anglo-Maratha War

zones.text: Ahmedabad, Gwalior and Salsette, the ground taken in the war

wars.outcome: Treaty of Salbai (17 May 1782): both sides returned the territory captured in the war; Salsette stayed with the Company from the Treaty of Purandhar (1 March 1776), which 'annulled that of Surat' but, on the page, left the British the revenues of Salsette and the Broach districts.
wars.note: Years 1775-1782: the Treaty of Surat (6 or 7 March 1775) to the Treaty of Salbai (17 May 1782), First_Anglo-Maratha_War. Repair: the war had no zone and cited the British_Empire page.

wars.name: Second Anglo-Mysore War
wars.outcome: The Treaty of Mangalore of 11 March 1784 restored the conquests on both sides (Dindigul and Karur to Tipu Sultan, Mount Dilly and the Calicut factory to the Company); no territory was ceded.
wars.note: Repair: terms read on the Treaty of Mangalore page (Articles 3 and 9); 'In 1783, the British took the town of Coimbatore'.

wars.name: Third Anglo-Mysore War

zones.text: the territories taken from Mysore, which 'deprived Mysore of much of its coastline'

wars.outcome: The Treaty of Seringapatam, 18 March 1792: about one half of Mysorean territory divided among the allies.
wars.note: The page names no district and no share by ally.

wars.name: Fourth Anglo-Mysore War
wars.outcome: Seringapatam falls in 1799 and Tipu Sultan is killed; much of Mysore is annexed by the British, the Nizam and the Marathas and the core restored to Krishnaraja Wadiyar III as a Company protectorate.

wars.name: Second Anglo-Maratha War

zones.text: Ahmednagar, the Doab and Delhi, Cuttack

wars.outcome: British victory (8 August 1803-24 December 1805): Cuttack from the Bhonsle (Deogaon, 17 December 1803), Haryana, the Doab, Delhi-Agra, parts of Bundelkhand, Broach and Ahmednagar from Scindia (Surji-Anjangaon, 30 December 1803); Holkar gave up Tonk, Rampura and Bundi (Rajghat, 24 December 1805).
wars.note: The Treaty of Bassein (December 1802) made the Peshwa a subsidiary ally before the war.

wars.name: Anglo-Nepalese War
wars.outcome: The Treaty of Sugauli (ratified 4 March 1816): Nepal lost Kumaon, Garhwal, the Western Terai and all Sikkim; the Mahakali became its western and the Mechi its eastern boundary; a British Resident was set up at Kathmandu.
wars.note: Some Terai lands were returned later in 1816; the infobox puts the western limit at the Sutlej, the text at the Mahakali.

wars.name: Third Anglo-Maratha War

zones.text: the Peshwa's, Bhonsle's and Holkar's dominions

wars.outcome: British victory (5 November 1817-9 April 1819): the Peshwa surrendered on 3 June 1818 and his territories were absorbed into the Bombay Presidency; the Saugor and Nerbudda Territories were formed; Holkar became subsidiary; Rajputana accepted British paramountcy.
wars.note: Treaties: Poona 13 June 1817, Gwalior 5 November 1817, Mandeswar 6 January 1818.

wars.name: First Anglo-Burmese War

zones.text: the Rangoon coast, Arakan, Assam and Tenasserim

wars.outcome: The Treaty of Yandabo of 24 February 1826: Burma cedes Assam, Arakan and Tenasserim, loses influence in Cachar and Jaintia and pays one million pounds.
wars.note: Manipur is listed as ceded in the body and as independent in the infobox.

wars.name: First Anglo-Afghan War

zones.text: Baluchistan: the Army of the Indus crossed the Bolan Pass and reached Quetta in March 1839, and Kalat was stormed on 13 November 1839

wars.outcome: 'The British forces left Afghanistan after recovering prisoners' and Dost Mohammad 'was released and re-established his authority in Kabul' (First_Anglo-Afghan_War, paraphrased: the page names no territorial result). The ledger carries Baluchistan as a hatched occupation from 13 November 1839 to 1841 (aligned with khanate-of-kalat).
wars.note: Repair: the war named durrani-empire, whose Cliopatria row ends in 1827; the states of the war are the Barakzai Emirate of Afghanistan (emirate-of-afghanistan, 1823-1926) and Shah Shuja's restoration (durrani-dynasty, 1839-1843). Zones added because the ledger occupies Baluchistan; dates follow khanate-of-kalat (1839/11-1841), not 1840-1842.

wars.name: British conquest of Sindh
wars.outcome: British victory, 17 February-24 March 1843 (Miani, Hyderabad): 'Annexation of Sindh into the Bombay Presidency within British India'.
wars.note: The page also describes a 1838 residency treaty and the isolation of the Amir of Khairpur by bribery and title.

wars.name: First Anglo-Sikh War

zones.text: the Sutlej frontier and the Punjab

wars.outcome: Treaty of Lahore (1846): 'Sikhs cede Jullundur Doab, Hazara, and Kashmir to the British'; Kashmir sold to Gulab Singh of Jammu (Treaty of Amritsar).
wars.note: Kashmir's sale is dated 1846 in the table and 1850 in the body.

wars.name: Second Anglo-Sikh War
wars.outcome: British victory; the Punjab and the North-West Frontier Province were annexed (1849-56 on the page).

wars.name: Second Anglo-Burmese War
wars.outcome: British victory; annexation of Lower Burma.
wars.note: Years 1852-53 are the page's; no day is given.

wars.name: Indian Rebellion of 1857

zones.text: the North-Western Provinces, Awadh and central India

wars.outcome: British victory (10 May 1857-20 June 1858): Delhi retaken in September 1857, Lucknow on 21 March 1858, Jhansi in March and Gwalior in June 1858; the Company was dissolved by the Government of India Act 2 August 1858.
wars.note: Hostilities were not formally declared ended until 8 July 1859. Hyderabad, Mysore, Travancore, Kashmir and the smaller Rajputana states stayed loyal ('breakwaters in a storm').

certainty.note: Company land is a scatter of districts, factories and client states; inland frontiers with the Marathas, Mysore and Awadh are approximate and Cliopatria's cells are coarse. The 1765 diwani and the 1792, 1803 and 1805 treaty cessions are sharp where the pages name the districts, but the pages mostly name no boundary.

Treaty and annexation borders: Sugauli (Mahakali and Mechi, 1816), Yandabo (1826), Sindh (1843), the Punjab (1849) and Lower Burma (1853) are fixed by treaty or annexation. The tribal and hill frontiers (Assam hills, the North-West Frontier, the Naga and Chin hills) and every princely-state boundary stay soft.

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 by sa-06-c. Cliopatria row 'British Empire' (1757-1858, 41 shapes). 14 pages opened in the first run (the budget), two of them wasted (the Anglo-Maratha Wars disambiguation page and the Umayyad 'Conquest of Sindh' article, both now dropped from sources). The repair of 2026-10-25 opened 38 further pages to apply the reviewer's fixes, so the page budget is exceeded on purpose.

WHAT THE ROW IS. Cliopatria's British Empire 1757-1858 is the East India Company's India with its protected states, plus a few stray Canadian cells. Its Q8680 id is shared with British Colonial Empire (1706-1999), the global aggregate owned by eu-11: they are different states drawn from one Wikipedia page ('British Empire' describes one empire and draws no line between them), so this dossier keeps only the 1757-1858 row and does not merge the aggregate. The slug and the Cliopatria Name stay 'british-empire' because gwalior-state, indore-state, kingdom-of-nagpur, hyderabad-state, nawab-of-awadh, kingdom-of-mysore, sikh-empire, nepal, nawabs-of-bengal and the sa-04-x Rajasthan dossiers name british-empire as their counterpart. The name and alt_names say what it is: the Company's rule, ended on 1 November 1858 (Cliopatria's British Raj row starts in 1859).

OVERLAP TO RESOLVE (for the orchestrator). The sa-06-x additions batch wrote history/polities/east-india-company.json (1600-1858, 99 events, cumulative new keyframes, 23 pages) for the same state and records the same gains and vassal tints; its notes ask for exactly this decision. This dossier reviews the 41 Cliopatria shapes against pages read here, and its ledger agrees with the east-india-company ledger wherever both opened a page (Plassey, Allahabad, Seringapatam 1792, Deogaon, Surji-Anjangaon, Sugauli, Yandabo, Sindh 1843, Punjab, Lower Burma, the vassals); it differs in a few years (Awadh vassal 1765 here against 1801 there; the Peshwa 1802; Berar is now 1853 here as there). In the repair the Kalat dates were aligned to 1839/11-1841 as east-india-company, khanate-of-kalat, bahawalpur-state and kingdom-of-coorg have them. The compile step must draw one of them, not both: the cleanest is to draw east-india-company's keyframes and ledger (richer, with months) and apply this dossier's verdicts to the Cliopatria shapes, or to list 'British Empire' in east-india-company's cliopatria_names and retire this file. Dropping this file needs the sibling counterpart strings changed.

CLIOPATRIA ERRORS FOUND (verdicts in keyframe_review). (1) Canada: 30-85 cells in Saskatchewan, Alberta, Manitoba, Ontario, the Northwest Territories, British Columbia and Quebec (bbox west to 125 W) in the 1788-1821 shapes; removed in every verdict (the cells vanish in 1822; no opened page says why). (2) The shape counts protected states as British: the Nizam's Hyderabad from 1799, Mysore's core from 1800, the Peshwa's lands from 1805, the Cis-Sutlej states from 1811, Rajputana, Holkar, Bhonsle, Cutch, Baroda from 1820, Bahawalpur from 1840, so its 3.63 M km2 in 1857-58 is 1.87 times the Company page's infobox 1,940,000 km2 for 1858 (direct rule). The ledger's vassal_start/vassal_end events carry the tints; the compile step must not draw the whole shape as direct rule. (3) Sindh (annexed 1843, client from 1838) is missing from the 1842-1845 shapes and back in 1846. (4) Baluchistan, 1,305 cells, is in the shapes from 1840 to 1858 although the First Anglo-Afghan War ended in 1842 and no acquisition there is on the Company page; removed from 1842 (a removal resting on page silence; the sibling khanate-of-kalat dossier has the British occupying Kalat 1839-1841 and the Treaty of Kalat only in 1876, which agrees). (5) Tenasserim, ceded at Yandabo in 1826, enters the shape only in 1853.
